source_inventory.title: Using Keywords & Mixed Keywords in Units

blocks.value: When using keywords, the following points apply:
• A unit has all the keywords of all models in that unit. A model only has its own keywords.
• If a rule specifies that it applies to a unit with a keyword, it applies to a unit which includes one or more models with that keyword.
• If a rule specifies that it applies to a model with a keyword, it only applies to a model with that keyword.

• If a rule specifies that it applies to ‘non-Keyword’ models/units, it only applies to models/units that do not have that keyword. For example, if a rule applies to non-Vehicle units, it only applies to units that do not have the Vehicle keyword.

• Some units can contain models that have different keywords. While this is the case, such a unit is considered to have all of the keywords of all of its models, and so is affected by any rule that applies to units with any of those keywords. Remember that attacks are made against units, not models.
• If a rule only applies to models with a specific keyword, then it instead only applies to models in such a unit that have the correct keyword.

• A rule with a comma-separated list of keywords, or a series of keywords separated by slashes ('/'), or two keywords separated by the word ‘or’ (e.g. ‘an Immortals, Deathmarks or Lychguard unit’) refers to a model/unit that has any one of those keywords.
• A rule with multiple adjacent keywords (e.g. ‘an Aeldari Guardians unit’) only refers to a model/unit that has all of those keywords.
• Some older rules use keywords without specifying model or unit: for example, MONSTER/VEHICLE or TRANSPORT. These rules refer to units with those keywords.
• Singular and plural instances of the same keyword function in the same way.
Models can move through different categories of terrain feature as follows:
• Exposed/Light: All models can move horizontally and vertically through exposed and light terrain features.
• Dense:
◦ INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/MOBILE models can move horizontally through dense terrain features.
◦ INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM models can move vertically through dense terrain features.

◦ Other models can move horizontally through dense terrain features provided that all sections of that terrain feature that the moving model’s base would move through are 2" or less in height. Otherwise, the moving model must move vertically to ascend or descend such sections. They cannot move through ceilings and floors while doing so, and they cannot end that move on any surface of that terrain feature that is not on ground level (see below).
MOVING VERTICALLY
Models can move vertically to ascend or descend terrain features. While doing so:
• That model must remain within ½" horizontally of that terrain feature.
• Add the distance moved vertically up, and the distance moved vertically down, to any other distance that model has moved since its unit began that move.
SETTING UP OR ENDING A MOVE

Models can be set up or end a move on the ground level of terrain features. Models can also be set up or end a move on any surface of a terrain featurethat is not on ground level, if all of the following apply:
• That model has one or more of the following keywords: INFANTRY/BEASTS/SWARM/FLY/MONSTER.
• After ending that move, that model is stable and no part of its base overhangs the outer edge of that surface.

value.title: Plunging Fire
value.body: As well as gaining superior lines of sight, models that ascend tall terrain features can benefit from the Plunging Fire rule (22.05).

blocks.value: An attached unit has all of the keywords of all of its component units. As such, an attached unit is affected by any rule that applies to units with any of those keywords. Note that models in an attached unit do not gain the keywords of other models in that unit that they do not already have. Remember that attacks target units, not models.

Example: An attached unit contains a leader model with the PSYKER keyword. While that model is part of that unit, that unit has the PSYKER keyword, even if the bodyguard models do not have that keyword. If that unit is attacked by a weapon with the [ANTI‑PSYKER 4+] ability, any unmodified wound roll of 4+ made against that unit is a critical wound, even if the attack itself is not allocated to that leader model.

requirements.summary: A rules unit possesses the union of its members' keywords.

evidence.proves: The attached unit includes its leader CHARACTER keyword while the bodyguard itself does not.

requirements.summary: A model possesses only its own keywords.

evidence.proves: The attached vehicle leader does not inherit the infantry members' Hidden condition.

requirements.summary: A keyword-qualified unit rule matches if any member has the keyword.

evidence.proves: The one PSYKER member causes a unit-keyword match.

requirements.summary: A keyword-qualified model rule matches only that model's own keywords.

evidence.assertion: assert tuple(('PSYKER' in model.keywords for model in unit.own_models)) == (False, False, True)
evidence.proves: Only the physical PSYKER member carries that keyword; siblings do not.

requirements.summary: A non-keyword rule matches only if the specified model or unit lacks that keyword.

evidence.proves: A prohibited keyword prevents the ability from applying.

requirements.summary: A mixed-keyword unit is affected by unit rules matching any member keyword.

evidence.proves: The one PSYKER member causes a unit-keyword match.

requirements.summary: Attacks target a rules unit, not a keyword-selected member.

evidence.proves: Enumerating separate bodyguard and leader identities produces one attached rules-unit target; allocation chooses models only after the unit is targeted.

qualifications: This proves target identity, with the adjacent keyword-union assertions covering keyword eligibility. It does not promote a keyword to every model.

requirements.summary: Model-keyword effects do not spill over to other models in a mixed unit.

evidence.proves: The model-scoped infantry condition does not grant Hidden to an attached vehicle.

requirements.summary: Comma, slash, and or keyword alternatives mean any listed keyword.

evidence.proves: Either MONSTER or VEHICLE in the slash-keyword list matches the same ability threshold.

requirements.summary: Adjacent required keywords form a conjunction.

evidence.proves: The Khorne Legiones Daemonica conjunction accepts the unit with both faction keywords and excludes the one missing Khorne.

requirements.summary: Legacy unspecified model/unit keyword subjects refer to units.
qualifications: Evidence gap: The typed keyword target is not inferred when model/unit is omitted; PSYKER is retained as unsupported residual language. The otherwise-identical explicit PSYKER unit form is parsed separately as a positive control. See tests/order97_gap_probes_01_08.py and observed_gaps_01_08.json, finding implicit-unit-keyword-consumer-boundary.

requirements.summary: Singular and plural spellings identify the same canonical keyword.
qualifications: Gameplay gap: keyword-sequence normalization preserves distinct CHARACTER and CHARACTERS tokens, and the real unit target gate rejects the plural while accepting the singular on the same CHARACTER model. The pinned keyword probe exercises the keyword itself, not pluralized model-owner labels. Resolve singular/plural aliases at the source boundary and retain canonical runtime identity.

requirements.summary: All models may traverse Light terrain horizontally and vertically.

evidence.proves: A Mounted model passes through a Light feature above the generic two-inch threshold.
The Light Vehicle case passes through a four-inch feature along a vertical witness.

requirements.summary: All models may traverse Exposed terrain horizontally and vertically.
qualifications: Gameplay gap: selected-source Exposed lacks an explicit typed category or verified source alias; the exact exposed token fails closed. See probe_exposed_category.

requirements.summary: Infantry, Beasts, Swarm and Mobile may pass horizontally through Dense features.

evidence.proves: The model-keyword terrain matrix exercises horizontal permissions.

requirements.summary: Infantry, Beasts and Swarm may pass vertically through Dense features.

evidence.proves: Infantry, Beasts and Swarm each pass vertically through a four-inch Dense wall.

evidence.assertion: assert any((s.vertical_distance_inches > 0 for s in result.segments))
evidence.proves: The witnessed accepted transit contains actual vertical movement.

requirements.summary: Otherwise Dense horizontal traversal is allowed only through sections at most two inches high.

evidence.proves: The two-inch wall is traversable without added height.
An ineligible Vehicle cannot pass through the tall wall.

requirements.summary: Other models must ascend and descend taller Dense sections.

evidence.assertion: assert any((segment.traversal_mode.value == 'climb' for segment in matching_segments))
evidence.proves: The permitted route climbs the actual tall Dense volume.

requirements.summary: Models without vertical Dense transit permission cannot pass through ceilings or floors while climbing.
qualifications: Gameplay gap: a Vehicle passes vertically through a thin Dense floor at three inches; see probe_dense_floor_crossing.

requirements.summary: An unqualified model cannot end its move on an elevated terrain surface.

evidence.proves: The Vehicle upper-floor endpoint is explicitly rejected.

requirements.summary: Ascending or descending models remain within half an inch horizontally of the feature.
qualifications: Gameplay gap: a real vertical path more than half an inch from all terrain is accepted by TerrainPathLegalityContext; no ascending/descending contact gate is applied.

requirements.summary: Count both upward and downward travel in the total distance budget.

evidence.proves: Ascending three inches and descending three inches adds six vertical inches.
The vertical total is added to horizontal travel.

requirements.summary: Ground-level endpoints are allowed; elevated surfaces require Infantry, Beasts, Swarm, Fly or Monster.

evidence.proves: Permitted model keywords can use supported upper endpoints.
Other keywords cannot use upper endpoints.

requirements.summary: An elevated endpoint must be stable and its base must not overhang.

evidence.proves: Overhanging upper-floor endpoint is rejected.
The shared endpoint owner rejects overhang beyond a rotated floor.

nonoperative_blocks.reason: Traversal group labels and illustration title.
Examples illustrate the category, climbing and endpoint rules.
Plunging Fire callout points to 22.05 without modifying these movement rules.

requirements.summary: The attached unit has the keywords of all current component models for unit-targeting rules.

evidence.proves: The attached target has CHARACTER despite a non-Character Bodyguard.

requirements.summary: An individual model does not inherit another component model’s keywords.

evidence.proves: Only the actual Psyker specialist contributes to a model-keyword-gated roll.
The Bodyguard component does not acquire CHARACTER from its attached Leader.

nonoperative_blocks.reason: Illustrative instance of the separately enumerated operative rule; no additional permission or restriction.
